answers.question: I want to be ready for the 5K in November. Should I run every day next week to get there faster?
answers.answer:
No, please do not run every day next week. Your legs, tendons and feet are still meeting running for the first time, and the gains come while you rest between sessions, not during them. Running daily this early is the fastest way to a sore shin or Achilles that costs you weeks.

Three run days with a rest or walk day in between is the right dose for now. We will grow the time you spend running inside each session first, then add a fourth day later in the block when that feels easy. Ten weeks is enough runway to get you across the 5K line without walking, as long as we build it brick by brick.

new.analysis:
You did the hardest part: you started, and you finished every session feeling proud and pain-free. That is the foundation we build on.

The pattern I want this week is the same three days, each a little longer, with the run portions growing before the walk portions shrink. Monday and Wednesday stay around 25 minutes so your legs get a known dose twice before the longer Saturday. Saturday stretches to 30 minutes and is where we first try running 90 seconds and walking 60, so your lungs and legs learn a slightly longer continuous effort.

Keep every run at a pace where you could speak in short sentences. If the calves feel tight before a run, walk the first five minutes before you start the intervals, and keep the dog walks gentle on the day after each run. Sleep around seven hours and the easy effort are both doing real work for you here.
